candidate_relations.reason: Both medulloblastoma and RGNT can present as fourth-ventricle masses in young adults with obstructive hydrocephalus, but they are entirely different diagnostic entities. RGNT is characteristically a well-demarcated, homogeneous, non-enhancing, non-calcified lesion in a young adult—features consistent with this case. Medulloblastoma is a high-grade embryonal tumor that typically shows contrast enhancement and more aggressive imaging features. The clinical and imaging profile (34-year-old, no enhancement, homogeneous, well-demarcated) favors RGNT over medulloblastoma. The candidate shares the correct anatomical location but asserts an incompatible tumor subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Medulloblastoma is a distinct malignant embryonal tumor of the fourth ventricle/cerebellum, not a rosette-forming glioneuronal tumor (RGNT), which is a WHO grade I mixed glioneuronal neoplasm

case_quality_flags: RGNT is a rare WHO grade I tumor; imaging features (no enhancement, homogeneous, well-demarcated, young adult) are classic and help distinguish from medulloblastoma
